issues.legal_issue: A grant covering less than an entire village qualifies as an estate only when the grant is expressly of the named village and the excluded lands satisfy the statutory conditions for exclusion.
material_facts: The original grant was unavailable, and the claim that the land formed part of an estate rested on incomplete entries in an inam register.

The entries indicated that most of the village area had been granted to one holder and a smaller area to another under separate personal grants; they did not establish that the main grant covered the whole village.

The evidence did not satisfactorily establish that the grant was expressed as a grant of the named village or that the excluded area had previously been granted on a qualifying tenure or reserved for communal purposes.
issues.conclusion: The grant was not proved to be a grant of a whole village or a grant of a named village with qualifying excluded lands; the land therefore was not an estate under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(2)(d) of the Madras Estates Land Act, an inam village means a whole village granted in inam, not merely a substantial part of a village. Explanation 1 permits a grant expressed to be of a named village to qualify despite excluded lands only if those lands fall within the stated categories. The claimant bears the burden of establishing estate status. The Court relied on Janakirama Sastri v. Jagani Gopalam for the construction of “any inam village.” The judges differed on whether “other tenure” should be limited by ejusdem generis to tenures like service tenure or could include personal inams; the evidence did not establish the necessary prior exclusion either way.

rule.if: inam_estate_classification_case and grant_did_not_cover_entire_village and (not grant_expressed_as_named_village or not excluded_lands_proven_previously_granted_or_reserved)

predicates.inam_estate_classification_case: The proceeding requires the court to decide whether land qualifies as an estate under the applicable land-tenure definition.
predicates.grant_did_not_cover_entire_village: The evidence shows that the grant covered less than the entire area of the village.
predicates.grant_expressed_as_named_village: The grant expressly describes itself as a grant of the named village, rather than a grant of a specified area within it.
predicates.excluded_lands_proven_previously_granted: The evidence establishes that lands excluded from the grant had already been granted on a qualifying tenure or had been reserved for communal purposes.
predicates.land_is_not_an_estate: The land does not qualify as an estate under the applicable definition.

issues.definition: When an estate-classification proceeding concerns a grant that did not cover the whole village, the land is not an estate if the grant was not expressly of the named village or the required status of the excluded lands was not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant does not acquire a permanent statutory right of occupancy in land unless the land qualifies as an estate under the governing statute.
material_facts: The respondent leased the land for a fixed term and claimed a permanent right of occupancy under the statute after the lease expired.
The respondent relied on the proposition that the land was part of an estate, but the evidence did not establish that status.
The suit concerned the landholder’s request for an injunction against interference with its possession after expiry of the lease.
issues.conclusion: Because the land was not established to be an estate, the respondent was not entitled to a permanent right of occupancy under Section 6(2); the appeal was allowed and the trial court’s order restored.
issues.legal_principle: Section 6(2) of the Madras Estates Land Act did not confer the claimed permanent right of occupancy where the land was not an estate within Section 3(2)(d).

predicates.statutory_occupancy_claim_case: A tenant claims a permanent right of occupancy under a statute governing rights in estate land.
predicates.land_not_established_as_estate: The evidence in the proceeding does not establish that the land qualifies as an estate.
predicates.tenant_has_no_permanent_statutory_occupa: The tenant is not entitled to a permanent statutory right of occupancy in the land.

issues.definition: A tenant claiming statutory permanent occupancy has no such right when the proceeding does not establish that the land qualifies as an estate.
